physics_goals.quote: A promising technology concept for sub-GeV dark matter detection is described, in which low-temperature microcalorimeters serve as the sensors and superfluid $^4$He serves as the target material.
physics_goals.value: Direct detection of sub-GeV dark matter with a superfluid helium target and calorimetric readout

summary.plain: HeRALD is a dark matter detector that uses a small bath of superfluid helium, cooled to near absolute zero, and superconducting sensors that detect both flashes of light and individual helium atoms boiled off the surface. It is part of TESSERACT and is proposed for the Modane underground laboratory.
summary.technical: Helium Roton Apparatus for Light Dark matter: superfluid 4He target (nuclear recoils of sub-GeV dark matter) read out by TES calorimeters sensing prompt and triplet scintillation and quasiparticles (phonons and rotons) via quantum evaporation of helium atoms and their van der Waals adsorption on the sensor; Cs film stopping keeps the sensor dry. Prototype HeRALD v0.1 (~10 g): 145 eV threshold (5 sigma), sensitivity to masses down to 220 MeV/c^2. Proposed host: LSM as a TESSERACT module.
